title: Career Roadmap: Policy Analyst
summary: Analyse public policies, government programmes and socioeconomic issues to develop evidence-based recommendations for governments, research institutions, think tanks and development organisations.

facts.Current degree: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies (BA / B.Sc Liberal Arts & Sciences)

about.label: Education Pathway
about.text: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies – Politics, Philosophy & Economics (PPE)

blocks.text: Analyse public policies, government programmes and socioeconomic issues to develop evidence-based recommendations for governments, research institutions, think tanks and development organisations.

rows.text: Any stream; Economics, Political Science, Mathematics and Sociology are useful
Liberal Arts degree with a Politics, Philosophy & Economics (PPE) major
Public policy, governance, development studies, public finance or international relations
Master's in Public Policy, Economics, Development Studies, Political Science or Public Administration

blocks.text: A PPE degree combines political institutions, economic reasoning and ethical analysis, making it relevant to policy research. Quantitative methods and research experience strengthen employability.

blocks.label: Policy Research
blocks.text: Literature reviews, policy briefs and stakeholder analysis.

blocks.label: Political & Economic Analysis
blocks.text: Government institutions, public finance, incentives and regulatory frameworks.

blocks.label: Data Analysis
blocks.text: Excel, statistics, survey analysis and introductory Python or R.

blocks.label: Research Methods
blocks.text: Qualitative interviews, comparative analysis and programme evaluation.

blocks.label: Communication
blocks.text: Clear writing, evidence-based arguments and presentations.

blocks.label: Critical Thinking
blocks.text: Assessing trade-offs, implementation barriers and unintended consequences.
Build three or four policy-focused projects:

blocks.label: Policy Brief
blocks.text: Recommend improvements to a policy in education, healthcare, employment or urban development.

blocks.label: Comparative Policy Study
blocks.text: Compare how two states or countries address the same issue.

blocks.label: Public Data Analysis
blocks.text: Examine a socioeconomic indicator using reliable official datasets.

blocks.label: Programme Evaluation
blocks.text: Create an evaluation framework with measurable outcomes.

blocks.label: Stakeholder Analysis
blocks.text: Map affected groups, institutions, incentives and implementation risks.
For each project, distinguish evidence from assumptions and cite reliable sources.
Target opportunities at:

items.text: University policy and economics research centres.
International development and public affairs organisations.

blocks.text: Look for Policy Research Intern, Research Assistant, Programme Analyst Intern, Legislative Research Intern and Public Affairs Intern roles.
Prioritize:

items.text: Excel, Power BI, R or Python for data analysis.
GIS fundamentals for regional, urban or environmental policy.

blocks.text: A portfolio of policy briefs and analytical projects is more useful than accumulating unrelated certificates.
Policy Research Intern
Research Associate / Junior Policy Analyst
Policy Analyst / Programme Analyst
Senior Policy Analyst → Policy Lead / Research Director
Progression depends on research quality, domain expertise, experience and the recruitment criteria of the organisation.

rows.text: Select a policy domain and study existing policies, official reports and datasets.
Write one policy brief and complete a small quantitative or comparative policy project.
Build a research portfolio, prepare a policy-focused résumé and apply for internships or junior research roles.

blocks.label: Target-ready profile
blocks.text: Strong policy research, economic and political reasoning, data literacy, concise writing and a portfolio demonstrating practical, evidence-based recommendations.
